items.descriptionTR: Mining has been the lifeblood of this remote Congolese hill town for decades. Now, it is fueling the spread of a devastating virus. ⁂ Aid agencies are racing to help health workers in the Democratic Republic of Congo. The virus is known to have killed at least 84, but the true toll may be far higher. ⁂ The vaccine development process and coordination between health organizations have improved since a devastating 2014-2016 outbreak. ⁂ Our chief Africa correspondent, Declan Walsh, reports from the epicenter of the Ebola outbreak on how the gold mining industry and the outbreak are linked. ⁂ In a remote mining town at the center of the Democratic Republic of Congo’s Ebola outbreak, grief and mistrust are complicating efforts to stop the virus. Health workers are trying to treat the ill and bury the dead, but some residents are still in denial that the disease is even real.
items.titleTR: The Gold Mines at the Heart of This Ebola Outbreak ⁂ What to Know About the Ebola Outbreak ⁂ The World Has Learned From the Last Ebola Outbreak, but Gaps Remain ⁂ How Ebola Spreads Through Gold Mining ⁂ Mistrust Spreads With the Ebola Virus in Congo
